messages.content: You preferred local processing because it gave more control and you expected it to be faster. A controlled benchmark now shows the remote service is twice as fast, but the local option still works offline and keeps the data on the machine. How does that change your position?

I would revise the performance part of the position: the remote service is clearly faster in this benchmark. I would not discard the local option entirely, because the offline and on-device-data advantages are still intact. I would now prefer remote processing when speed dominates, and local processing when those control constraints matter more.

messages.content: You favored option A because it was simpler to maintain and supposedly cheaper. Verified pricing now shows A and B cost the same, while A is still simpler for this team. Do you still prefer A?

Yes, but for a narrower reason. I would drop the cost argument because the verified pricing removes it. I would still prefer A for this team on maintainability alone, unless that simplicity turns out to be too small to matter in practice.
